CITY OF LA VERNE
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE
  Wednesday, March 10, 2021

1.  Chairperson Simison called the regular meeting of the La Verne Planning
  Commission to order at 6:30 p.m. He stated that all comments should be sent to
  planning@cityoflaverne.org.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chairperson Simison led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL: Planning Commissioners present: Thomas Allison, Jeff Allred,
  Jason Lorge, Phil May and Jason Simison. Advisory personnel present:
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer, City Attorney Bob Kress,
  Planning Intern Gabriel Rivera and Secretary Natalie Hiatt.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  There was one public comment received.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

6.  CASE NO. 22-21ZA – DRAFT SHORT-TERM RENTAL ORDINANCE

  RESOLUTION NO. 1271

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING CASE NO. 22-21ZA, AN ORDINANCE TO MODIFY TITLE
  18 OF THE LA VERNE MUNICPAL CODE RELATING TO SHORT-
  TERM RENTAL UNITS.

  Planning Intern Gabriel Rivera presented his staff report.

  Chairperson Simison opened the Public Hearing.
 Planning Commission Minutes
March 10, 2021
  There was one public comment received via email.

  Chairperson Simison closed the Public Hearing.

  The Commissioners proceeded to ask questions regarding a “Host Stay” rental.
  They also discussed the number of occupants allowed and the annual renewal
  process.

  Staff answered the Commissioner’s questions and discussed modifying the
  language in regards to the permit renewal process.

  It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner May to
  approve Case No. 22-21ZA with an amendment to the guidelines. Motion carried
  by a 5-0 vote.

OTHER MATTERS/INFORMATION

  None

ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:18 p.m. The Planning Commission will meet at
  an adjourned meeting to be held on March 17, 2021 at 6:30 p.m.

  ____________________________________________
  Chairperson, Planning Commission

  ATTEST:

  _________________________________
  Secretary, Planning Commission

March 10, 2021
From: Linda Lockhart Wilkinson [mailto:ldlchannel@verizon.net]
Sent: Wednesday, March 10, 2021 5:34 PM
To: Planning; Linda Lockhart Wilkinson
Subject: Fwd: SHORT TERM RENTAL RESOLUTION NO.:1271
Good afternoon Planning Commission,

I’d like to thank you for approving my relocation request of the historic house and
bungalow at the corner of White Avenue and 1st Street to their forever home at
1st and F Streets. Once the craftsman style house on White Avenue is relocated,
I intend to use it, a portion of the time, as a short term rental. It will be the
premium jewel in the short term rental market.

I own and manage short term rentals in several cities with over a thousand
reservations behind me, almost 500 reviews as a host and several dozen as a
guest around the world. I coined my business “The Living Simply Collection –
Stylish Short Term Rentals.” Attached are photos of some rentals in the
Collection.

Each city has different parameters and restrictions with Palm Springs by far the
most restrictive and punitive, the more lenient, Big Bear, and Pasadena,
somewhere in between. The other differentiation in rentals is the draw to the
area. The majority of short term renters in La Verne have a family or friend in the
area or connection to one of the local universities or businesses. It's a rarity for
guests to vacation in La Verne.

The proposal to set a threshold of allowing neighbors to determine if a property
owner may rent out their unit for 30 days or less is extremely subjective, allows
undue prejudice and financial burden if an applicant must spend $1,500 to file for
a Conditional Use Permit for not passing the popularity of neighbors.
The ability to rent should be a revocable privilege based upon performance or
lack thereof. 3 Substantiated complaints within a 12 month period should be
grounds to revoke the privilege to rent short term for 2 years. All host applicants
should be treated equally until given reason otherwise.

The key to running a successful short term rental that ensures the peaceful use
and enjoyment of surrounding homes is response time when there is an issue.
These issues include extra guests not on the reservation, loud music or voices,
too many cars (1 vehicle per rented bedroom is a good threshold,) a barking dog,
leash law violation etc. The optimum guideline is that which mandates an owner
or manager to respond to the property within 30 minutes, day or night, to a police
or code enforcement call. The response presence is the key to keeping harmony
between short term rentals and neighbors and does not correlate to an owner or
manager sleeping at the property. The proposal to have an owner reside on the
property is ambiguous as to how it’s applied. Does it mean an owner or their
designated agent cannot work or must be at the property if a renter is present at
all times? Please consider proper management verses residence in the
ordinance.

  4
 Planning Commission Minutes
March 10, 2021
I don't care for long term rentals of 30 days or more. There is a huge gamete in
the wear and tear on the property with longer rentals verses those of a few days.
The other reason I prefer short term, typically 2 to 5 nights, is because guests do
not get too comfortable and push the limits in the House Rules by doing such
things as inviting friends over. Another advantage is that the houses are not
always occupied so the places are spotless and very well maintained. There's
nothing worse that getting the keys back from a long term tenant and finding
thousands of dollars in repairs and damage.

There are certain standards that each of my short term rentals have to ensure
respect for our neighbors. One is a Ring Doorbell and/or security system with
video recording of people and noise notification sent to my cell phone 24 hours a
day. If the reservation is for 3 guests, only 3 are seen in the video. I don’t allow
others than those stated on the reservation without my prior written approval. If
there is any outdoor amplified music, I will address the noise before it disturbs a
neighbor. Each confirmed guest receives information regarding the amenities
and house rules which includes the statement in bold letters “if guests violate a
house rule, owner at her sole discretion reserves the right to terminate their
reservation without credit or refund. ” Prior to pandemic times, I would require
guests staying at my short term rentals to meet upon arrival and acknowledge in
writing that they have received and understand the House Rules.

I ask that consideration be given to include the following in the ordinance:

    All short term rentals must have a current City of La Verne Business
  License and post the license number on any and all advertisements.
    All short term rentals must have a local owner, property manager or
  responsible party that can respond to any urgent police request or
  emergency within 30 minutes.
    . The number of guests per a house rented may not exceed 2 persons
  per bedroom plus 1. Therefore, a 2 bedroom house may accommodate 5
  persons and a 3 bedroom would accommodate 7 guests. Children over
  the age of 3 count as guests;
    . Occupants of short-term rentals are limited to those stated when the
  reservation is made and no others;
    . All rentals must be properly insured for liability purpose as a rental;
    . All rentals must have properly functioning smoke and carbon monoxide
  detectors along with an easily accessible fire extinguisher;
    . Any property with a pool must have a self closing gate to the pool area.
  Any and all doors leading directly into an area around a pool shall have a
  door alarm with a chime when opened.
    . The number of guests per rented room (not applicable rental of an
  entire house) may not exceed 3 with proper beds. Guests may not sleep
  on the floor;
    ; No amplified outdoor music or loud voices that may be heard at the
  property line;

    . The number of cars is restricted by the number of bedrooms if off street
  parking is not available. On street parking should be limited to 1 car per
  rented bedroom.
    Guests with pets must obey leash laws and pick up after their
  animals;
    .  No use of illicit drugs or excessive use of alcohol;
    Rental of individual bedrooms without the owner residing on premises
  is prohibited unless permitted and licensed as a motel, hotel or “bed and
  breakfast.”
    . If the premises are not owner occupied, rental of a bedroom in an
  apartment or condominium must be allowed under the master rental
  agreement between the owner and tenant. If condo is owner occupied,
  short term rentals must not be restricted under the HOA and
    3 Substantiated violations of the above within a 12 month
  period should be grounds to revoke the privilege to rent short term
  for 2 years.

Kindly confirm receipt.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Linda Lockhart Wilkinson

32 year La Verne resident
